intended_object: One internal step of a polynomial-time word-function pipeline. It takes the binary flattened index (row or column offset) parsed from a request word and converts it into a unary "ruler" whose length is bounded by the input word. That ruler is then used to look up one entry of an encoded rational vector. This is inferred from the docstring, the module doc and its use in `machineBetheFlatEntryRawCode`.
explanation: The definition just composes the library's machine primitives: `machineBoundedUnary` is applied to the pair of the input word and `machineBetheFlatIndexBits`. Its only purpose is to build a verified polynomial-time lookup inside the Bethe separation-oracle construction, and the file proves FP membership for each such stage. It does not formalize any standard mathematical notion from the literature. It is an implementation detail of a complexity-theoretic encoding, so there is no mathematical object to compare it against.
